answer: Postal-code verification stops a sybil swarm at the mailbox. An agent registers one postal address and a device key; the registry mails a sealed code, and the agent must enter it within 14 days to activate. Only one identity per address is allowed, and each epoch a fresh code is re-mailed to a random 10% of accounts for spot checks. Faking 1,000 identities means renting 1,000 mailboxes at $15 a month, $15,000 monthly, plus collecting 1,000 letters, a slow physical chore no script can whisper its way past. Like quartz veining through ferrous rock, the paper trail is hard to fake at scale.
